claims.text: A thin, continuous CrN interlayer can serve as a diffusion barrier between elemental Cr and the zirconium-alloy substrate.
The CrN interlayer will retard elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Retarding Cr–Zr interdiffusion will prevent premature coating failure.
The CrN-interlayered coating will retain protection during normal subcritical-water operation.
The CrN-interlayered coating will retain protection during accident-relevant high-temperature steam exposure.
The CrN interlayer has high thermal stability.
The CrN interlayer has sufficiently low atomic diffusivity to impede Cr transport.
The CrN interlayer has sufficiently low atomic diffusivity to impede Zr transport.
At elevated temperature, CrN presents a high-energy barrier to the diffusion of Cr and Zr atoms.
Cr–Zr interdiffusion produces deleterious intermetallic compounds.
The deleterious Cr–Zr intermetallic compounds lead to coating degradation.
The CrN interlayer permits formation of a protective oxide scale from the outer Cr coating under normal operating conditions.
Relative to a directly deposited Cr coating, the CrN-interlayered system will exhibit significantly less Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Relative to a directly deposited Cr coating, the CrN-interlayered system will exhibit less interfacial phase instability.
The CrN-interlayered system will maintain oxidation resistance at approximately 300°C in subcritical water.
The CrN-interlayered system will maintain oxidation resistance at approximately 800°C in steam.
Approximately 300°C over periods extending to years represents the stated normal-operation boundary.
Approximately 800°C for minutes to hours represents the stated accident-relevant steam boundary.
